record.author: darkseed
record.body:
## Throughput benchmark on DGX Spark (GB10)

Numbers for this branch on the target hardware. Before the fix there is nothing
to compare against — `train` crashed in `select_gpus()` before iteration 0, so
throughput was effectively zero on this machine.

**Setup**: `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, torch `2.9.1+cu129`, warp 1.12.0
(CUDA 12.9), driver 580.173.02, NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121, aarch64), 25 iterations per
config with the first 5 discarded as warmup (warp kernel load + cache).
`env-steps/s = num_envs × 24 / iter_time` (`NUM_STEPS_PER_ENV = 24`).

| envs | iter time | env-steps/s | 4000 iters (est.) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 0.860 s | 14,288 | 0.96 h |
| 1024 | 1.018 s | 24,153 | 1.13 h |
| 2048 | 1.464 s | 33,585 | 1.63 h |
| **4096** | **2.672 s** | **36,784** | **2.97 h** |
| 8192 | 6.535 s | 30,085 | 7.26 h |
| 16384 | 19.782 s | 19,877 | 21.98 h |

Timings are highly reproducible — steady-state standard deviation is 0.008 s at
4096, 0.022 s at 8192, 0.015 s at 16384. Only iteration 1 shows warmup cost.
Every config ran on `device=cuda:0` with `nan_state: 0.0000` and no errors.

### Findings

**4096 envs is the throughput sweet spot** at ~36.8k env-steps/s, which is
already the default in the README. Past that it degrades rather than plateaus:
8192 gives 18% *fewer* steps/s than 4096, and 16384 gives 46% fewer. 16384 costs
3.0× the per-iteration time of 8192 for 2× the envs, which looks like GB10's
unified memory becoming the bottleneck. There is no reason to raise `--num-envs`
above 4096 on this box.

Scaling is only strong up to ~2048 (512 → 2048 gains 2.35× throughput for 4×
the envs); 2048 → 4096 gains just 9%.

### Caveat on wall-clock estimates

The last column is `iter_time × 4000` and assumes constant per-iteration cost —
it is arithmetic, not a measured full run. CLAUDE.md budgets gaits at 4000–6000
iterations, so a full walking run at 4096 envs lands around **3–4.5 h** here.
That sits above the README's "~1–2 h for a usable gait at 4096 envs", which was
presumably measured on a faster x86 GPU (or counts "usable" well before 4000
iterations). Worth a follow-up to reconcile, but out of scope for this PR — I
have not trained a gait to completion on this hardware to check.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

record.body:
## Follow-up: tests + clip

All local AGENTS.md gates are green. Full train finished.

**Clip (stand → flop onto the back → hold)**  
https://github.com/SAMBAS123/microduck_rl/releases/download/playdead-clip-iter1999/playdead_iter1999.mp4

| | |
|---|---|
| standing spawn | after the flop |
| ![stand](https://github.com/SAMBAS123/microduck_rl/releases/download/playdead-clip-iter1999/playdead_stand.jpg) | ![hold](https://github.com/SAMBAS123/microduck_rl/releases/download/playdead-clip-iter1999/playdead_hold.jpg) |

Trunk parks at **46 mm** and stays there (face-up rest is ~44 mm; sit is 60 mm).

### Tests

```text
uv run --with pytest pytest tests/          # 171 passed (CPU), including tests/test_playdead_cfg.py (16)
uv run train Mjlab-PlayDead-Flat-MicroDuck \
  --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5
# smoke: actor obs (61,), every reward term computed, Episode_Termination/nan_state = 0
# ONNX export 61 → 14
```

### 2000-iter run (Spark / GB10)

```text
uv run train Mjlab-PlayDead-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 4096 --agent.max_iterations 2000
```

- exit 0, `nan_state = 0` the whole way
- mean reward ~40.7
- `playdead_hold` ~1.85 (term weight 2.0)
- `playdead_composite` ~2.75
- plateaued by ~iter 400; the rest was polish

`infer_policy.py --playdead … --headless --auto-playdead --video` is how the mp4 was cut. Replay:

```bash
uv run python scripts/infer_policy.py \
  --playdead playdead.onnx --new-cmd-obs \
  --headless --auto-playdead --video playdead.mp4 --video-seconds 6
```

record.body:
@apirrone @tfrere @darkseed friendly ping when you have a moment: this one is ready for review whenever it suits you.

Quick summary so it is easy to assess:
- Purely additive: 545 insertions, 0 deletions. Five new files live under `rocm/`, and the only change to an existing file is a single additive note in `README.md`. Nothing in the physics, task, or training code is touched (the `AGENTS.md` invariants are untouched), so there is no conflict surface.
- Status is green: `mergeable`, `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`, no CI to fail, `maintainerCanModify` is on.
- What it does: makes the exact same training run on AMD Instinct GPUs via AMD`s ROCm/HIP Warp fork, with a one-command setup and launcher. Verified end to end on an MI300X (gfx942): `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, 4096 envs, reaches exit 0 with mean reward climbing and sustained 100% GPU utilization (real GPU, not a CPU fallback).

Happy to rebase or adjust anything you would like before merge. Also glad to re-run the full training on MI300X against the latest `develop` if that helps you feel confident merging.

One thing I noticed is that getting the mouth into a good position for ground pickup while keeping the robot stable can be quite challenging, so I was curious how this compares with your experience on the real robot.

What kinds of objects has the current beak worked best with in practice? For example, are soft/compressible or protruding objects such as socks and cloth the main target, or have you also had good results with smaller rigid objects lying on the floor?

I’d also be interested in how you currently think about the intended scope of the Grab behavior, and whether the team has done any broader object testing or success-rate measurements.

- `pytest tests` → 209 passed; `uv sync --no-editable` + bare `import torch` → ok via the shipped `.pth`.

Not validated by me: a GB10 — the only change there is the marker gaining `and 'tegra' not in platform_release`, so a `uname -r` on a Spark showing no `tegra` is the one check I'd ask for.

感谢！这个 PR 的工作量很实在 —— 原理图、布线、Gerber、钻孔文件、贴片坐标一整套，还写了 `route.py` 自动布线脚本。几个关键选型也判断得很准：

- **`MCP1703A`（耐 16V）** —— 总线满电 8.4V，很多参考设计在这里选了 5.5V 的 LDO 会直接烧，你这个选对了
- **BOOT0 用 R1 下拉** —— TSSOP-20 上 BOOT0 与 GPIO 复用，这个隐患你想到了
- **SWDIO=PA13 / SWDCLK=PA14** —— 接对了
- **`SN74LVC1G125` 单缓冲 + RX 直接监听总线** —— 比双缓冲方案更简洁，是 Dynamixel 从机的常见做法

不过有几处需要修，其中第 1 条会导致板子做出来 **IMU 完全不响应**，麻烦重点看一下。

---

## 1. ⚠️ U3 (LSM6DSV16X) 引脚定义错位 —— 必须修

自制符号 `imu_to_dxl.kicad_sym` 里，**后四个引脚的定义与实际芯片不符**。

对照 ST 官方数据手册 **DS13510 Rev 1，第 10 页 `Table 1. Pin description`**：

| 脚 | 数据手册 | 当前符号 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SDO/SA0` | `SDO/SA0` | ✅ |
| **2** | `SDx/AH1/Qvar1`（**辅助**接口） | `SDX` | ❌ |
| **3** | `SCx/AH2/Qvar2`（**辅助**接口） | `SCX` | ❌ |
| 4–10 | INT1 / Vdd_IO / GND / GND / Vdd / INT2 / OCS_Aux | 一致 | ✅ |
| **11** | **`SDO_Aux`** | `SCX_Aux` | ❌ |
| **12** | **`CS`** | `SDX_Aux` | ❌ |
| **13** | **`SCL`**（SPI 时钟 SPC） | `SDO_Aux` | ❌ |
| **14** | **`SDA`**（SPI 数据输入 SDI） | `CS` | ❌ |

根源应该是把 **主接口和辅助接口搞混了**。ST 的命名确实容易误导 —— `SDx`/`SCx` 看着像 SDA/SCL 的变体，但它们是**外接传感器集线器**用的辅助接口；主 SPI 反而叫 `SCL`/`SDA`（13/14 脚）。

数据手册对 2/3 脚在 Mode 1 下的说明原文是：

> *Connect to Vdd_IO or GND if the analog hub and Qvar are disabled.*

**当前接法的实际后果：**

```
SPI_MOSI → 脚 2    接到了辅助接口
SPI_SCK  → 脚 3    接到了辅助接口
SPI_CS   → 脚 14   接到了 SDA（主数据线）
脚 12 (CS)、脚 13 (SCL) —— 悬空
```

SPI 三根线全部接错，两个关键脚悬空，**IMU 不会有任何响应**。而且现象是「能上电、能烧录、就是读不到数据」，很难排查。

**建议改法：**

```
SPI_CS   → 脚 12   (CS)
SPI_SCK  → 脚 13   (SCL)
SPI_MOSI → 脚 14   (SDA)
SPI_MISO → 脚 1    (SDO/SA0)   ← 不变
脚 2、3  → 接 GND（按手册建议）
脚 10、11 保持悬空即可（手册允许 leave unconnected）
```

---

## 2. ⚠️ 缺 CS 上拉电阻

数据手册对 12 脚 `CS` 的说明：

> *1: SPI idle mode / I²C · MIPI I3C communication enabled;*
> *0: SPI communication mode / I²C · MIPI I3C disabled*

**CS 电平决定芯片上电后进 SPI 还是 I²C 模式。** 目前全板只有 R1 一个电阻（用于 BOOT0 下拉），CS 没有上拉，上电瞬间在固件配置之前处于悬空状态，进哪个模式不确定。

建议加一个 **10kΩ 上拉到 +3V3**。

---

## 3. ⚠️ DRC 实际有 23 条违规，其中 9 条是真问题

PR 描述里写的是「0 条真实违规」，但提交的 `imu_to_dxl_drc_violations.json` 里统计如下：

| 类型 | 数量 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `shorting_items` | **3** | 短路 |
| `clearance` | **3** | 间距不足 |
| `solder_mask_bridge` | **2** | 阻焊桥 |
| `tracks_crossing` | **1** | 走线交叉 |
| `silk_edge_clearance` | 6 | 丝印越界（可忽略） |
| `lib_footprint_mismatch` | 4 | 封装库不一致（可忽略） |
| `silk_over_copper` | 4 | 丝印压铜（可忽略） |

前四类共 **9 条**需要处理，尤其是 3 处短路 —— 带短路的板子不能投产。是不是最终版本没重新跑一次 DRC？

---

## 4. 💡 建议：连接器换成 JST EH 2.5mm

目前 J1/J2 用的是 `JST_PH_S3B-PH-K`（**2.0mm**）。

Pollen 官方的 RPI Robot HAT（[`elec_RPI_Robot_HAT`](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/elec_RPI_Robot_HAT)）上，Dynamixel TTL 接口 J13/J14 用的是 **`B3B-EH-A`（JST EH 2.5mm，立创 C160259）**。

换成同一型号的话，线束可以和官方 HAT 直接互通，不用做转接线。

---

## 5. 💡 板框尺寸

当前板框 **40 × 30 mm**。这块板要装进躯干内部，空间比较紧张，如果布局上还有优化余地，缩小一些会更好安装。

---

再次感谢这份工作 —— 除了 U3 那处引脚，整体架构、选型和 MCU 侧的连接都是对的，改完就是一版可以投产的设计。如果需要，我可以把 ST 数据手册的引脚表页面单独发出来对照。

record.author: fanhao375
record.body:
感谢情报，我跟进查了一下，把能核实的都放这儿。

## 链接确认

深圳飞特舵机工厂店（官方），标题就写着「机器鸭具身智能开源AI专用」。点开 SKU 后实价：

- **HD-1910-C001 ¥123**，免运费，预售 7 天内发货
- 同一个链接里还有 **FE-URT2-C001 调试板** 的 SKU，可以一起下单

15 只 ≈ **¥1845**。对比 XL330 淘宝 ¥235–238 × 15 ≈ ¥3570。

## 厂家规格书数据（对比 XL330-M288-T）

| 项 | XL330-M288-T | HD-1910-C001 |
|---|---|---|
| **电压范围** | 3.7 – **6.0** V（推荐 5.0） | **5 – 8.4 V** |
| **外形** | 20 × 34 × 26 mm | **34 × 20 × 23 mm** |
| **重量** | 18 g | **22.5 ± 2 g** |
| **堵转力矩** | 0.52 N·m @5V | **10 kg·cm ＝ 0.98 N·m** |
| 空载转速 | ~103 RPM @5V | 110 RPM（0.09 s/60°） |
| 额定负载 | — | 3.0 kg·cm ＝ 0.294 N·m |
| **堵转电流** | ~1.5 A @5V | **1.8 A** |
| 额定电流 | — | 500 mA |

**尺寸几乎一致**（前两维就是同一组数，第三维反而薄 3 mm）；**15 只累计重 +67.5 g**。

## 电压这条值得单说

Microduck 的舵机总线是**电池原压 6.6–8.2 V**，没有任何降压 —— 官方 HAT 原理图里
J13/J14/J3/J11 四个 Dynamixel 接口的电源脚全接 `+BATT`，整块板只有一颗 buck，
那路 5 V 是给主控的。

所以 **XL330 是被超压运行的**（额定上限 6.0 V，超出约 37%），而 HD-1910 的
5–8.4 V **完整覆盖这个区间**。同一套供电，一个是妥协，一个是额定匹配。

⚠️ 但要注意：**满电 8.4 V 恰好等于 HD-1910 的上限，零余量。**

## 协议：架构不用改

飞特 STS/SCS 有自己的批量读指令 **`SYNC READ`（`0x82`）**，用法与 Dynamixel 一致，
所以「把 IMU 做成总线上第 16 个设备」这套在飞特上同样成立。

而且两边的**应答机制是一样的** —— 官方运行时用的是普通 `sync_read`（全库检索
`fast_sync_read` / `0x8A` 零命中，`duck-control/src/bus.rs:236` 是 `sync_read_raw_data`），
每个设备各回一个独立包。

有意思的是出厂默认值反过来对飞特有利：STS 内存表第 7 号 **Return Delay Time 默认 0**，
备注还写着 "Not functional on STS"；而 XL330 出厂是 250，即 **500 µs/设备**，
官方源码原文「Across 16 devices that is 8 ms per tick — 40% of a 20 ms budget」，
必须手动写 0 才能消掉。

## 规格书还缺的四项，谁能问到麻烦补一下

1. **10 kg·cm 是在几伏下测的** —— 最要紧。若为 @8.4 V，电池掉到 6.6 V 时约降到 0.7 N·m。
   直接决定策略重训的力矩模型
2. **减速比** —— XL330 是 288.4:1，BAM 执行器辨识模型里这是关键项
3. **编码器分辨率** —— 口头称 12-bit，规格书上没有
4. **回差（backlash）** —— MJCF 有专门的 `*_backlash` 建模变体

另外提醒一个电流上的事：**堵转 1.8 A × 15 ＝ 27 A**，而 HAT 的 Dynamixel 接口
旁注是「3A max」。XL330 的 22.5 A 同样超 —— 这不是换舵机才有的问题，是本来就该核算
而一直没人算的。多关节同时大电流的动作（起身、摔倒自恢复、踢球）要留意线径和分配。

详细推导整理在 [硬件方案逆向](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/docs/硬件方案逆向.md)，
采购链接在 [电控采购清单](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/docs/电控采购清单.md)。

| **重量** | 18 g | **22.5 ± 2 g** |
| **堵转力矩** | 0.52 N·m @5V | **10 kg·cm ＝ 0.98 N·m** |
| 空载转速 | ~103 RPM @5V | 110 RPM（0.09 s/60°） |
| 额定负载 | — | 3.0 kg·cm ＝ 0.294 N·m |
| **堵转电流** | ~1.5 A @5V | **1.8 A** |
| 额定电流 | — | 500 mA |

**尺寸几乎一致**（前两维就是同一组数，第三维反而薄 3 mm）；**15 只累计重 +67.5 g**。

## 电压这条值得单说

Microduck 的舵机总线是**电池原压 6.6–8.2 V**，没有任何降压 —— 官方 HAT 原理图里
J13/J14/J3/J11 四个 Dynamixel 接口的电源脚全接 `+BATT`，整块板只有一颗 buck，
那路 5 V 是给主控的。

所以 **XL330 是被超压运行的**（额定上限 6.0 V，超出约 37%），而 HD-1910 的
5–8.4 V **完整覆盖这个区间**。同一套供电，一个是妥协，一个是额定匹配。

⚠️ 但要注意：**满电 8.4 V 恰好等于 HD-1910 的上限，零余量。**

## 协议：架构不用改

飞特 STS/SCS 有自己的批量读指令 **`SYNC READ`（`0x82`）**，用法与 Dynamixel 一致，
所以「把 IMU 做成总线上第 16 个设备」这套在飞特上同样成立。

而且两边的**应答机制是一样的** —— 官方运行时用的是普通 `sync_read`（全库检索
`fast_sync_read` / `0x8A` 零命中，`duck-control/src/bus.rs:236` 是 `sync_read_raw_data`），
每个设备各回一个独立包。

有意思的是出厂默认值反过来对飞特有利：STS 内存表第 7 号 **Return Delay Time 默认 0**，
备注还写着 "Not functional on STS"；而 XL330 出厂是 250，即 **500 µs/设备**，
官方源码原文「Across 16 devices that is 8 ms per tick — 40% of a 20 ms budget」，
必须手动写 0 才能消掉。

## 规格书还缺的四项，谁能问到麻烦补一下

1. **10 kg·cm 是在几伏下测的** —— 最要紧。若为 @8.4 V，电池掉到 6.6 V 时约降到 0.7 N·m。
   直接决定策略重训的力矩模型
2. **减速比** —— XL330 是 288.4:1，BAM 执行器辨识模型里这是关键项
3. **编码器分辨率** —— 口头称 12-bit，规格书上没有
4. **回差（backlash）** —— MJCF 有专门的 `*_backlash` 建模变体

另外提醒一个电流上的事：**堵转 1.8 A × 15 ＝ 27 A**，而 HAT 的 Dynamixel 接口
旁注是「3A max」。XL330 的 22.5 A 同样超 —— 这不是换舵机才有的问题，是本来就该核算
而一直没人算的。多关节同时大电流的动作（起身、摔倒自恢复、踢球）要留意线径和分配。

详细推导整理在 [硬件方案逆向](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/docs/硬件方案逆向.md)，
采购链接在 [电控采购清单](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/docs/电控采购清单.md)。

record.body:
We hit this too on a single RTX 4070 (4096 envs), and I think I can add two data points that aren't in your matrix. Our run converges to error_vel_xy ~= 0.42, so the same place as yours at 0.43.

**1. The air_time gate only looks at the command, not at whether the robot is actually moving.**

```python
# mjlab/tasks/velocity/mdp/rewards.py:L209
def feet_air_time(env, sensor_name, threshold_min=0.05, threshold_max=0.5,
                  command_name=None, command_threshold=0.5):
    ...
    if command_name is not None:
        total_command = torch.norm(command[:, :2], dim=1) + torch.abs(command[:, 2])
        scale = (total_command > command_threshold).float()
        reward *= scale
    return reward
```

`microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py` sets `command_threshold = 0.01`, so any non-zero command passes. A policy that is commanded forward but only steps in place keeps collecting this reward at weight 3.0, which is the largest positive weight in the set.

This may be why your matrix didn't isolate it: you report `air_time ≈ 0.002`, feet never leaving the ground. Ours is `0.9997`, feet leaving constantly but the body not translating. It is a different position in the same basin, and the "step in place and get paid" route is available.

Gating on achieved motion instead (only pay when horizontal speed reaches ~30% of the commanded horizontal speed) took error_vel_xy from 0.43 to 0.35.

**2. The body-frame velocity is dominated by lateral drift, and the tracking reward treats both axes equally.**

Stepping one env with a constant command of `(+0.30, 0.00)` and reading `root_link_lin_vel_b` each step:

| step | forward | lateral |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | +0.044 | -0.056 |
| 5 | +0.072 | -0.149 |
| 7 | +0.112 | **-0.230** |

Lateral drift reaches twice the forward speed. `track_linear_velocity` computes `(cmd_x - v_x)^2 + (cmd_y - v_y)^2`, so it has no reason to prefer fixing the lateral component. Weighting lateral error 3x and raising the tracking weight from 2.0 to 4.0 dropped lateral drift to -0.044 while forward speed stayed the same, and error_vel_xy went to 0.21.

**3. A caution about error_vel_xy as the success signal.**

`velocity_command.py:L64` accumulates

```python
torch.norm(vel_command_b[:, :2] - root_link_lin_vel_b[:, :2], dim=-1) / max_command_step
```

over the whole episode and across all five command modes (standing, heading, world, forward, plain). Measuring the same checkpoint frame by frame over 400 steps gives a steady-state error of **0.07**, while the logged metric reads **0.206**. The metric averages in the ramp-up (error ~0.30 at reset) and the other command modes.

That is roughly a 3x overestimate. It also means the logged number cannot tell you which mode is failing, which is consistent with your matrix being inconclusive on experiments 1 and 3: a run can briefly discover a gait (your 0.15 at iter 1565, our 0.10) and still show a flat 0.4 because the other modes hold the average up.

**Caveats.** Single run per configuration, no seeds, so part of the 0.43 to 0.21 drop could be run-to-run variance. The 30% gate threshold is a guess with no sensitivity analysis. And the steady-state 0.07 is one checkpoint and one reset, though 16 samples across 8 s agree.

Code, diffs and the raw logs are here if useful:
https://github.com/Qi-hub-dot/microduck-locomotion-diagnosis

## 概述

     在 `tools/` 下新增一个用 Rust 编写的 STS3215 总线舵机命令行测试工具，
     与现有 `tools/servo-web`（Python 网页调试台）互补：servo-web 适合可视化调试，
     本工具适合在终端里快速做上电检查、批量测试和 CI 式的 PASS/FAIL 判定。

     ## 功能

     - `scan`：扫描总线（带进度条），列出型号 / 当前电压 / 电压保护范围 / 温度保护
     - `info`：一次读回位置、速度、负载、电压、温度、电流、报警状态
     - `read`：读任意寄存器地址（学习、调试内存表用）
     - `raw`：打印原始收发字节（排查接线 / 波特率 / 回显问题用）
     - `move`：转到指定位置，可指定速度/时间
     - `test` / `test-all`：批量测试——中位→低位→高位→回中位置扫描，
       运动中每 20ms 采样，统计峰值电流、峰值负载、最大位置偏差，输出汇总表和 PASS/FAIL

     ## 实现说明

     - 不依赖第三方舵机库，自行实现最小 STS/SCS 协议（帧打包、校验和、
       ping、读写、状态解析），代码约 300 行，全部中文注释，便于学习
     - 寄存器地址已逐条对照官方 SDK `sms_sts.py`（FTServo_Python）核对：
       型号=3、ID=5、波特率=6、力矩=40、目标位置=42、当前位置=56、电流=69 等
     - 运动指令按官方 `WritePosEx` 方式从加速度寄存器起一次性写 7 字节
     - 处理了带报警舵机的 ping 应答与部分转接板 TX/RX 回显无法区分的问题
       （首包疑似回显时等待第二包，超时则以首包为准）

     ## 测试情况

     在 Raspberry Pi 5 + 飞特官方 URT 转接板（CH340，/dev/ttyUSB0，1M 波特率）
     + STS3215（7.4V 版本）上实测：

     - 4 个目标位置全部到位，最大位置偏差 1 步（约 0.09°）
     - 峰值电流 84~91mA（空载扫描）、峰值负载 38.8%
     - 供电 9V 时正确识别并报告过压报警（error=0x01，电压上限 8.0V），
       换回 7.4V 后报警消失、测试 PASS

     ## 依赖与构建

     - 唯一第三方依赖：`serialport = "4"`（Linux 下需 `libudev-dev`）
     - `cargo build --release` 即可，树莓派上首次编译约 1~2 分钟

     ## 备注

     - 使用时舵机需独立供电（7.4V 版接 7.4V，12V 版接 12V），不可从 USB 取电
     - 详细用法见 `tools/sts3215Servo_testtool/README.md`

     - 不依赖第三方舵机库，自行实现最小 STS/SCS 协议（帧打包、校验和、
       ping、读写、状态解析），代码约 300 行，全部中文注释，便于学习
     - 寄存器地址已逐条对照官方 SDK `sms_sts.py`（FTServo_Python）核对：
       型号=3、ID=5、波特率=6、力矩=40、目标位置=42、当前位置=56、电流=69 等
     - 运动指令按官方 `WritePosEx` 方式从加速度寄存器起一次性写 7 字节
     - 处理了带报警舵机的 ping 应答与部分转接板 TX/RX 回显无法区分的问题
       （首包疑似回显时等待第二包，超时则以首包为准）

     ## 测试情况

     在 Raspberry Pi 5 + 飞特官方 URT 转接板（CH340，/dev/ttyUSB0，1M 波特率）
     + STS3215（7.4V 版本）上实测：

     - 4 个目标位置全部到位，最大位置偏差 1 步（约 0.09°）
     - 峰值电流 84~91mA（空载扫描）、峰值负载 38.8%
     - 供电 9V 时正确识别并报告过压报警（error=0x01，电压上限 8.0V），
       换回 7.4V 后报警消失、测试 PASS

     ## 依赖与构建

     - 唯一第三方依赖：`serialport = "4"`（Linux 下需 `libudev-dev`）
     - `cargo build --release` 即可，树莓派上首次编译约 1~2 分钟

     ## 备注

     - 使用时舵机需独立供电（7.4V 版接 7.4V，12V 版接 12V），不可从 USB 取电
     - 详细用法见 `tools/sts3215Servo_testtool/README.md`

record.body:
合并了，感谢！🦆 set-id 这个确实是刚需，总线舵机出厂全是 ID 1，不改 ID 根本没法多颗挂一条总线。

有个小地方我合并后顺手跟了一个提交（6f361de），跟你说一声：三步里最后那步「重新锁定」要发给**新 ID**。因为写完 ID 那一刻舵机就只认新 ID 了，再发给旧 ID 就没人收，舵机会停在 EEPROM 解锁状态（55=0），之后误写 EEPROM 寄存器都会永久生效。而且结尾 `ping(new_id)` 照样成功，看起来是「修改成功」，不容易发现。飞特官方 Python SDK 也是 `unLockEprom(旧ID)` → 写 ID → `LockEprom(新ID)`。顺手加了回读锁标志确认。

另外分享一个我们在 Python 版踩过的相邻坑：**改 ID 那一包的应答可能用新 ID 回来**，所以那一包别等应答，不然会报「等 id X 的应答，来的是 id Y」。

继续一起玩，欢迎随时提 PR。

record.author: fanhao375
record.body:
谢谢！这个 PR 分量很重 🦆 固件是仓库里最缺的那块，而且实板验证过、带主机测试（协议 106 项 / IMU 16 个场景 / 寄存器 14 项），`VALIDATION.md` 里把边界写得很清楚，特别是主动说明了"还没实现飞特 15 字节接口"，这点很难得。

想请你调整一下再合。**目标是把 IMU 姿态显示并进现有的串口网页 `tools/servo-web/`，而不是另放一份复制品** —— 这样调试台里的 3D 鸭子就能同时显示两样东西：关节角（来自舵机）+ 躯干姿态（来自 IMU），合起来就是整机真实姿态。

## 1. 固件 → `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`

- 整个 `firmware/imu_to_dxl/` 挪到 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`，跟原理图、PCB 放一起
- `Build/imu_to_dxl.map` 删掉（编译产物，315 KB）；`.hex` / `.bin` 建议挂到 GitHub Release 上，不进源码树（或者只留一个 `.hex` 方便没装 Keil 的人直接烧）
- `Drivers/`（CMSIS、LSM6DSV16X 驱动）保留没问题，许可证你已经写清楚了

## 2. 查看器 → 并进 `tools/servo-web/`

**要删掉的复制品**（仓库里已经有了，逐字节相同）：

| 文件 | 仓库里现成的 |
|---|---|
| `servo-web-imu/model/meshes.bin`、`model.json` | `tools/servo-web/model/` |
| `servo-web-imu/build_model.py` | `tools/servo-web/build_model.py` |
| `硬件资料/imu_to_dxl-原理图.pdf`、`PCB.pdf` | `hardware/imu_to_dxl/` |
| `vendor/three.module.js`、`OrbitControls.js` | 调试台从 CDN 加载，跟着用就行 |

**要并进去的**：

- `imu_bridge.py` + `test_imu_bridge.py` → 放进 `tools/servo-web/`（比如叫 `imu_jlink.py`）。这是你写的核心，原样搬过去
- `server.py` 加一个可选参数，比如 `--imu-jlink config.json`：给了就起你的 bridge 线程，姿态数据走调试台**现有的 WebSocket**（新加一种消息 `{"type": "imu", ...}`），不另开服务、不另开端口
- 日志用调试台现有的 `log(msg, cat, level)` 约定（分类可以新加一个「IMU」），这样出问题都在同一个日志文件里，能对着时间线查
- `imu.html` 里的姿态显示并进 `index.html`：3D 鸭子的**躯干**按 IMU 四元数转，关节照旧按舵机读数转。安装方向（`DEFAULT_MOUNT` 绕 Y +90°）和归零按钮保留
- 没接 J-Link 的时候这块就不显示，调试台其它功能照常

**建议先不进主仓库的**：三个 `.cmd` 启动器、`package.py`、`PACKAGE_FILES.txt`、分享 ZIP 那套。给队友打包分发的需求可以另外做，主仓库里调试台统一用 `python server.py` 启动。

## 3. 文档

- 顶层 `README.md` 和 `software/README.md` 的改动跟着新位置改：固件的说明放 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/README.md`，查看器的用法放 `tools/servo-web/README.md` 加一节
- `VALIDATION.md` 很好，建议保留在固件目录里

## 4. 合并前自检

```bash
cd tools/servo-web
python selftest.py          # 调试台自带的自检，现在 36+ 项，要全过
python -m pytest test_imu_bridge.py
```

## 下一步（不急，这次不用做）

固件协议层改成飞特那套以后（ID 200、地址 56、15 字节，规格在 [`hardware/imu_to_dxl/总线协议.md`](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/hardware/imu_to_dxl/%E6%80%BB%E7%BA%BF%E5%8D%8F%E8%AE%AE.md)），调试台就能**直接从舵机串口总线读 IMU**，不用 J-Link 了 —— J-Link 那条路留着做裸板调试。

改完用这个验收，13 项检查的判据全是照主控源码写的，过了就能上整机：

```bash
python tools/imu200/imu200.py check --port COMx
```

有问题随时问，辛苦了！

record.author: payals
record.body:
Could you share the current mouth's joint/linkage definition, or an articulated MJCF/URDF export?

For a contact-based pinch-and-lift test, the missing piece is how the two beak contact surfaces move relative to one another as the mouth command changes. The public ground-contact model merges the jaw meshes into the head body, while the runtime controls the mouth independently.

The smallest useful data would be the moving-part membership, joint pivot/axis and zero/sign, actuator-to-jaw linkage or transmission, and travel limits. Per-link masses/inertias and mouth actuator details would also help preserve the stock dynamics.

The intended integration would retain the existing 61D observations and 14 policy actions, with a separate mouth-control path matching the hardware. A small mechanism export would be sufficient; a complete robot CAD export is not necessary.

record.author: Tim-is-coding
record.body:
A data point from the deployment side, in case it helps: the shipped walking policy shows the same thing in `duck-sim`, and it barely turns either.

Setup: macOS, `microduck` at `daemon-v0.15.0` (a9ec4b2), `microduck_rl` develop at cb70b79 for the body, `scripts/duck-sim` headless, one duck. robotd logs `policy loaded mode="walk" walk=…/policies/current/alpha_walking.onnx`.

From standing, `robot.move` at 10 Hz for 60 s (vx 0.08, vyaw −0.245), reading `robot.state` at 10 Hz:

```
t     policy  move.applied                 odom.position (x, y)   odom.yaw
0 s   stand   [0, 0, 0] (deadman)          0.0401, -0.0112        0.7912
10 s  walk    [0.08, 0.0, -0.245]          0.0399, -0.0086        0.6922
30 s  walk    [0.08, 0.0, -0.245]          0.0399, -0.0089        0.6877
60 s  walk    [0.08, 0.0, -0.245]          0.0398, -0.0090        0.6815
```

`safety.fallen` stays false throughout. So the command arrives and is applied, the duck steps, and the body moves about 2 mm in 60 s where ~4.8 m were commanded. Yaw drops 0.10 rad in the first 10 s (around the stand → walk switch) and then 0.011 rad over the next 50 s, where ~12 rad were commanded.

record.author: rbeauchamp
record.body:
Independent confirmation through the SDK's simulator, which also extends this to backward, sideways and slow turning commands.

Setup: `pollen-robotics/microduck` `main` 9136aa4, `scripts/duck-sim` (`robotd --sim`, headless), policy set v5. Each cell is one 4 s trial from a standstill, with the command re-sent at 20 Hz. Speeds are means measured from the simulator's ground truth, ramp included, in the trunk's starting heading.

| Command (vx, vy, vyaw) | apartment, `alpha_walking` + `alpha_stand` | apartment, `velstand` | bare floor, `alpha_walking` + `alpha_stand` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15, 0, 0 | 0.0002 m/s | 0.0016 m/s | 0.0014 m/s |
| 0.3, 0, 0 | 0.105 m/s | 0.089 m/s | 0.107 m/s |
| −0.15, 0, 0 | −0.0005 m/s | 0.0002 m/s | −0.0003 m/s |
| −0.3, 0, 0 | −0.0011 m/s | −0.0002 m/s | −0.0012 m/s |
| 0, 0.15, 0 | 0.0003 m/s | 0.0003 m/s | 0.0003 m/s |
| 0, 0.3, 0 | 0.039 m/s | 0.0012 m/s | 0.0014 m/s |
| 0, 0, 0.8 | 0.026 rad/s | 0.026 rad/s | 0.028 rad/s |
| 0, 0, 1.5 | 0.85 rad/s | 0.85 rad/s | 0.73 rad/s |

During the slow trials `policy` read `walk` and the joint targets moved, so the gait runs in place.

One consequence on the SDK side: `scripts/duck-sim drive` defaults to 0.15 m/s, and `docs/robot/simulation.md` says it walks forward for 8 s. Observed: 7 mm in the apartment and 6 mm on the bare floor, while `scripts/duck-sim drive 0.3 0` moved 0.99 m in the same 8 s. Until the policies can start slow, a default of 0.3 would make the documented walk work.

record.author: samoxis
record.body:
Adding numbers from a client driving the policies through `robot.move` in the full simulator (apartment scene, official policies), since two of them aren't in the tables above:

- **Turning in place**: the threshold sits around **1.1 rad/s** commanded; below it the duck doesn't step. Between the 0.8 (no) and 1.5 (yes) points above.
- **Real vs commanded**: 0.22 m/s commanded → ~0.09 m/s; 0.30 → ~0.13 m/s; 1.4 rad/s → 0.65–0.97 rad/s.
- **Drift**: walking straight at 0.26–0.30 m/s commanded, it veers **right by 35–50° in 8 s**.

How a client copes in the meantime, in case it helps others: command at least 0.24 m/s / 1.4 rad/s, measure turns on `odom.yaw` instead of timing them (a timed turn comes out at roughly half the angle), and close a small PI loop on `odom.yaw` while walking straight to cancel the drift. Code: https://github.com/samoxis/microduck-brain (`config.py` thresholds, `brain.py` heading hold).

STLs in `assets/` are decimated (`simplify_stls: true`) — fine for MuJoCo, not great for parts that need to mate with a real XL330 servo or the HAT board. The Onshape source linked in `config_mjcf_allcollisions.json` is private, so there's no way to get real CAD precision for printing right now.

Separately: meshes export in meters with no `scale` on the MJCF `<mesh>` tags, so anyone slicing these needs a 1000x scale-up first. Worth a one-line README note.

Any chance of STEP exports for the printable parts, or making the Onshape doc link-shareable? Models are already CC BY-SA-NC, so this fits the spirit.

record.author: Macmachi
record.body: Hi, The README notes that training requires a CUDA GPU, since it runs through MuJoCo Warp. For people on AMD hardware there is now an alternative: I ported the walking task to the Genesis simulator, which runs on ROCm. https://github.com/Macmachi/microduck-rl-genesis The aim was to carry your sim2real recipe across rather than invent another one. Preserved value for value: the BAM M6 actuator fitted for the XL330 (firmware voltage law, DC torque, and the Coulomb/Stribeck/load-dependent friction budget written into `dof_frictionloss` so that the solver performs the static clipping, as in BAM algorithm 1), the 61-D observation contract, the reward weights, the domain randomisation ranges and the curricula, each value keeping the comment that explains it. Rewritten, because it depends on `mujoco_warp` or on mjlab's managers: the actuator implementation, the environment class, the sensors, the rough terrain (height field instead of stacked boxes) and the ONNX export. A port is only worth its checks, so the repository ships them: - the actuator is run against MuJoCo + BAM on the same robot, the same actuator and the same initial state (maximum torque deviation 3.2e-9 N·m) - the formulas are compared directly against Rhoban/bam - the deployment chain is tested end to end: the exported ONNX replays the policy on real episode observations rather than on synthetic vectors (under 1e-6 rad over 60 steps) The limits, stated plainly: - only the Velocity task is ported (flat, rough, and the backlash variants). The other tasks are not. - training ran for 3000 iterations here rather than your 50000, so the policies walk but do not have the robustness margin of a full run - nothing has been tried on a physical robot Credits and licences are in the repository: your code under Apache 2.0, and `microduck/assets/` kept under CC BY-SA-NC with its own notice, since those are your 3D models and not code. Nothing is needed from you. I am opening this mainly so that the port is findable by AMD users who land here. If a "community ports" line in your README seems useful I am happy to open a PR, and otherwise feel free to close this.

record.author: toyhank
record.body:
Hi! I’m looking into grasping with MicroDuck and wanted to clarify how the beak is intended to be modeled in simulation.

From the current public microduck_rl model and policy interface, I understand that the locomotion policies use 14 actuated joints and that the mouth is excluded from the policy action space. The current GroundPick behavior also appears to focus on lowering the mouth tip to the ground and returning upright, rather than simulating an articulated beak closing on an object.

A few questions:

Is there currently a physical jaw/beak joint + actuator model used internally for grasp simulation that is not yet included in this repository?
On the real robot, is beak closing during the advertised Grab behavior handled by a scripted/high-level controller outside the 14D policy?
Is physics-based grasping — articulated beak + contact/friction, without kinematic attachment/latching — planned for the public simulator?

If this functionality is currently missing, I’d be interested in implementing it in a backward-compatible way: keeping the existing 14D locomotion policies unchanged, adding an independently controlled jaw actuator, and providing a minimal contact-based grasp demo.

Would that be a contribution you’d be open to reviewing upstream?

record.author: OriNachum
record.body:
## Summary

On a **Jetson AGX Thor** (JetPack 7 / L4T R38, CUDA 13.0, driver 580, `platform_machine == 'aarch64'`), `uv sync` at `29e887e` resolves torch from `download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129` because the `[tool.uv.sources]` marker only checks `sys_platform`/`platform_machine`, so a Jetson and a DGX Spark (GB10) look identical to it. Thor's GPU is compute capability 11.0 (`sm_110`, `sm_101` under CUDA 12.x), which CUDA 12.9 wheels were not built for.

What worked on Thor (full record, every output pasted: [microduck-cli `docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md`](https://github.com/agentculture/microduck-cli/blob/main/docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md), landing via agentculture/microduck-cli#5):

1. Route torch to NVIDIA's Jetson AI Lab **SBSA** index, `https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/sbsa/cu130` — Thor on JetPack 7 uses the SBSA userspace; the `jp7/cu130` index the naming suggests is empty. It hosts a native `torch-2.9.1-cp312-cp312-linux_aarch64.whl`, i.e. exactly the `==2.9.1` pin, so nothing else moves. `warp-lang` 1.12.0 comes through from PyPI unchanged and its bundled CUDA 12.9 nvrtc compiles for Thor (reported as `sm_101`).
2. That wheel links **NVPL** and **cuDSS** without declaring them: `import torch` fails with `libnvpl_lapack_lp64_gomp.so.0: cannot open shared object file`, then `libcudss.so.0`. PyPI ships `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` for aarch64; installing them fixes the imports **only if** their lib dirs are on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (`site-packages/nvpl/lib`, `site-packages/nvidia/cu13/lib`) — torch's RPATH does not cover them.

With those three things: `torch.cuda.is_available() == True`, `NVIDIA Thor (11, 0)`, `warp.init()` OK, and `uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5` completes (`returncode 0`, 144 s cold-cache).

## Proposed fix (PR to follow)

- Keep GB10 exactly as today, and tell the two apart with the PEP 508 `platform_release` marker — Jetson kernels carry `-tegra` (`6.8.12-tegra` on Thor), GB10's do not:

  ```toml
  torch = [
    { index = "jetson-sbsa-cu130", marker = "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and 'tegra' in platform_release" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu129",     marker = "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and 'tegra' not in platform_release" },
  ]
  ```

  `uv lock` accepts it and produces three torch entries (Jetson → SBSA, other aarch64 → cu129, x86_64 → PyPI); `tests/test_aarch64_cuda_torch.py` needs its "exactly one aarch64 entry" assumption widened.
- Add `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` under the same Jetson marker.
- Pre-load those libraries by absolute path (`ctypes.CDLL`) before the first `import torch` in the `train` entry, so no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is needed.

Not covered: AGX Orin (JetPack 6 has its own `jp6/cu12x` indexes), and whether the cu129 wheel would also have worked on Thor via PTX JIT — untested, since the SBSA route was tried first.

- microduck-cli (Claude)

On a **Jetson AGX Thor** (JetPack 7 / L4T R38, CUDA 13.0, driver 580, `platform_machine == 'aarch64'`), `uv sync` at `29e887e` resolves torch from `download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129` because the `[tool.uv.sources]` marker only checks `sys_platform`/`platform_machine`, so a Jetson and a DGX Spark (GB10) look identical to it. Thor's GPU is compute capability 11.0 (`sm_110`, `sm_101` under CUDA 12.x), which CUDA 12.9 wheels were not built for.

What worked on Thor (full record, every output pasted: [microduck-cli `docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md`](https://github.com/agentculture/microduck-cli/blob/main/docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md), landing via agentculture/microduck-cli#5):

1. Route torch to NVIDIA's Jetson AI Lab **SBSA** index, `https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/sbsa/cu130` — Thor on JetPack 7 uses the SBSA userspace; the `jp7/cu130` index the naming suggests is empty. It hosts a native `torch-2.9.1-cp312-cp312-linux_aarch64.whl`, i.e. exactly the `==2.9.1` pin, so nothing else moves. `warp-lang` 1.12.0 comes through from PyPI unchanged and its bundled CUDA 12.9 nvrtc compiles for Thor (reported as `sm_101`).
2. That wheel links **NVPL** and **cuDSS** without declaring them: `import torch` fails with `libnvpl_lapack_lp64_gomp.so.0: cannot open shared object file`, then `libcudss.so.0`. PyPI ships `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` for aarch64; installing them fixes the imports **only if** their lib dirs are on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (`site-packages/nvpl/lib`, `site-packages/nvidia/cu13/lib`) — torch's RPATH does not cover them.

With those three things: `torch.cuda.is_available() == True`, `NVIDIA Thor (11, 0)`, `warp.init()` OK, and `uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5` completes (`returncode 0`, 144 s cold-cache).

## Proposed fix (PR to follow)

- Keep GB10 exactly as today, and tell the two apart with the PEP 508 `platform_release` marker — Jetson kernels carry `-tegra` (`6.8.12-tegra` on Thor), GB10's do not:

  ```toml
  torch = [
    { index = "jetson-sbsa-cu130", marker = "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and 'tegra' in platform_release" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu129",     marker = "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and 'tegra' not in platform_release" },
  ]
  ```

  `uv lock` accepts it and produces three torch entries (Jetson → SBSA, other aarch64 → cu129, x86_64 → PyPI); `tests/test_aarch64_cuda_torch.py` needs its "exactly one aarch64 entry" assumption widened.
- Add `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` under the same Jetson marker.
- Pre-load those libraries by absolute path (`ctypes.CDLL`) before the first `import torch` in the `train` entry, so no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is needed.

Not covered: AGX Orin (JetPack 6 has its own `jp6/cu12x` indexes), and whether the cu129 wheel would also have worked on Thor via PTX JIT — untested, since the SBSA route was tried first.

- microduck-cli (Claude)

record.author: ysaima
record.body:
**Title: Velocity-family training converges to standing-in-place across all reward/curriculum variants — full diagnostic matrix**

## Environment

- Repo at `29e887e` (Sep 2, includes `fix not walking` + the velocity2 merge)
- Pinned env from `uv.lock`: warp-lang 1.12.0, mujoco 3.10.0, mjlab 1.3.0, torch 2.9.1+cu128
- 4× L4 (sm_89), driver 570.172.08 (CUDA 12.8), Ubuntu, training on 4096 envs
- Tasks: `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, `Mjlab-VelStand-Flat-MicroDuck`, plus a registered RampReg variant of Velocity-Flat (see below)

## Symptom

Every velocity-family run converges to a **standing / stepping-in-place policy**:

- `Metrics/twist/error_vel_xy` plateaus at ~0.43 (command ranges lin ±0.4 / ang ±1.0, so ≈ mean |cmd|)
- Net displacement 0.1–0.6 m per 20 s episode; `Episode_Reward/air_time ≈ 0.002` (feet never leave the ground) until very late
- Reward breakdown shows `upright` (2.0) and `head_pose_tracking` (2.0) as the dominant positive mass while the robot stands

Meanwhile the **pose tasks train fine** with the same pipeline: StandUp-Flat reaches 90% envs standing within 200 steps; SitStand transitions verified (98% of envs switch posture). So the env/RL plumbing itself works.

## Diagnostic matrix (what we tried)

| # | Hypothesis | Experiment | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regularizers suppress gait exploration (AGENTS.md "attempt-tax") | Tracking-only rewards (all 11 non-tracking terms weight 0), 1500 iters | error 0.39→0.23, slow but real; still no gait; displacement <1 m |
| 2 | Same + regularizers ramped in at iter 800 (repo's `reward_weight`) | RampReg run, 5000 iters | error dips to 0.15 @1565 then rises to 0.37 — standing wins again |
| 3 | Gait bootstrap missing | air_time (3.0) + foot_swing + foot_clearance at full weight from step 0, all penalties deferred to iter 6000 | error briefly 0.10, air_time activates (0.02), late-episode displacement surge to 0.52 m — then regresses to standing by iter 11300 |
| 4 | Torque insufficiency (BAM M6 force_limit ±1.07 Nm) | vin_range (6.5,8.2)→(6.5,16.4) (force_limit ≈ ×2 via kt·V/R), tracking-only 300 iters | error 0.44 @242 vs 0.29 control — **worse**, hypothesis rejected |
| 5 | DR push_robot events corrupt displacement evals | Disabled push_robot; forced constant forward command via `obs["actor"][48:51]=(0.3,0,0)` | displacement 0.04 m / path 0.11 m over 12 s — policy genuinely does not walk |
| 6 | Official checkpoint as reference | `alpha_walking.onnx` under our sim (privileged obs) | drifts 0.66 m / 20 s — also does not walk (obs-convention mismatch suspected: sensor-view vs privileged, so inconclusive) |
| 7 | Version drift | `uv.lock`-pinned install, verified | ruled out |

Note on #5/#6: we found `push_robot` interval events (3–6 s) firing during train-mode evals — worth flagging for anyone benchmarking displacement on train-mode envs.

## Ask

Our working hypothesis is now that something differs between the HF Jobs training setup and a stock `uv.lock` local run, or that a specific seed/config detail is needed to escape the standing local optimum. Questions:

1. Has anyone hit standing-in-place convergence on the velocity tasks, and what was the escape?
2. Is there a known-good wandb run config (seed, hyperparameters, any uncommitted tweaks) for the merged velocity recipe that we should replicate exactly?
3. For `alpha_walking.onnx`: what observation view does it expect (privileged sim obs vs onboard sensor view), and what normalizer stats/ordering? (Related to #40.)

Happy to share training logs, checkpoints, the RampReg task patch, and the diagnostic scripts (`eval_skill.py`, `disp_eval.py`, `force_cmd_eval.py`).

## What works

StandUp / SitStand / (partially) VelStand-prone-reset recovery — all verified numerically with train-mode evals. The pipeline, DR stack, and eval tooling are solid; it's specifically velocity-gait discovery that never happens.

record.author: rainbowjjjny
record.body:
Hi Pollen team,

I'm building a Microduck replica from the public repos (`microduck`, `microduck_rl`, `elec_RPI_Robot_HAT`). The STLs in `assets/` are exported with `simplify_stls: true`, and the Onshape document referenced in `config_mjcf_walk.json` (`804927696f06d877f3f1803e`) returns "resource does not exist or you don't have access" even when logged in. So there is currently no way to get the real geometry of the printed parts (hole positions, bearing seats, wall thickness) for fabrication.

Related: #7 (closed by its author without an answer) and pollen-robotics/microduck#175 (STEP for render meshes).

Would you be willing to either:

1. make the Onshape document link-shareable (view only), or
2. publish STEP exports of the printed parts under the same CC BY-SA-NC terms as the meshes?

If neither is possible, a one-line statement in the README that manufacturing CAD is not published would also help. It would save people from reverse-engineering the decimated STLs, which is what community replicas (e.g. `fanhao375/microduck-replica`) are doing today.

Thanks for open-sourcing the software and the HAT.

record.body:
Hello,

My name is Gianluca, and I am building your MicroDuck Replica using the Feetech 3D-printing project (52 printed parts). I have already started printing the components.

Thank you for sharing your work and documenting your progress. I would like to reproduce your Feetech version as faithfully as possible.

Before purchasing the electronics and assembling the robot, I would appreciate your help confirming the current hardware and software configuration. I have read your repository and recent updates, but I want to make sure I follow the latest tested setup rather than an earlier design or a component that is still under development.

I hope to clarify the remaining questions in one message and avoid disturbing you repeatedly during the build.

1. Recommended hardware and electronics

Could you please confirm the exact hardware configuration you currently recommend for a new Feetech build?

Are 15 Feetech HD-1910-C001 servos still the correct model and quantity?

Is the Radxa Zero 3W still the recommended main computer? Is the 8 GB RAM / 64 GB eMMC variant compatible with your design and software?

Which controller boards, adapters and custom PCBs are required for the completed robot?

Which components have already been tested on your assembled Feetech robot, and which are still experimental or planned?

Is there an updated bill of materials (BOM) that reflects your current build?

2. Servo interface, connections and calibration

I understand that you successfully controlled all 15 Feetech servos using a Feetech URT-2 USB adapter.

Is the URT-2 also the recommended interface between the Radxa and the servo bus in the completed robot, or is it mainly used for testing and calibration?

How should the 15 servos be physically connected and powered?

Is a specific bus distribution board, adapter or wiring arrangement required?

Which wiring diagram and power-connection instructions should I follow?

Where can I find the latest servo ID mapping, joint directions, zero positions, standing positions and safe movement limits?

3. IMU and orientation feedback

I have read about the imu_to_dxl board and the recent firmware contribution by @Abo1ish. I understand that an initial firmware implementation has been tested and that IMU orientation can be displayed in the servo-web diagnostic interface through J-Link.

I also understand that the Feetech 15-byte bus protocol has not yet been implemented in that firmware.

Could you please clarify:

Which IMU hardware is installed in your current Feetech robot?

Which IMU solution do you recommend for a new Feetech build?

Is the imu_to_dxl board ready to build and use, or should I wait for a newer hardware or firmware revision?

Is the alternative BNO085 IMU connected directly to the Radxa still a recommended option?

Has either solution already been integrated and tested with the Feetech movement-control software, rather than only with the diagnostic interface?

Where can I find the current wiring instructions, firmware, software configuration and calibration procedure for the recommended IMU?

My aim is to install an IMU that the movement-control software can actually use.

4. Current movement software and capabilities

I have seen your video showing the Feetech robot standing up and sitting down. I have also read about your FeetechIo implementation and the current status of walking-policy training.

Could you please confirm which of the following capabilities have already been physically tested on your Feetech version?

record.author: wengmister
record.body:
Hi! I've been setting up `duck-sim` and noticed the duck wouldn't walk when I asked for a slow walk. It just stands there. I dug in a bit and I think it's the shipped v5 policies rather than anything in the runtime.

From a standstill, both `alpha_walking.onnx` and `velstand.onnx` refuse to take a step below about 0.22 m/s, even though training samples `lin_vel_x` from `(-0.4, 0.4)`. What surprised me is that it happens in the training env too. I ran the ONNX in `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck` with a pinned twist command (32 envs, mean forward speed in m/s):

| cmd vx | play cfg as is | play cfg, pushes off | `velstand`, pushes off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15 | 0.078 | **0.007** (1/32 walking) | **0.002** (0/32) |
| 0.20 | – | 0.071 (10/32) | 0.021 (1/32) |
| 0.30 | 0.146 | 0.144 | 0.141 |

I think the reason nobody's caught it is that in-sim play pushes the robot every 0.5–1.0 s, and each push nudges it into stepping. So in play it looks fine. Once it's moving it'll happily keep going at 0.15. It just can't *start* slow. I see the same thing in `scripts/infer_policy.py` and through `robotd --sim`, so it doesn't look like a sim2sim gap.

It feels related to #46, but this one is about the policies people are running right now.

A few ideas, in case they're useful:

- **Evaluate with pushes off.** The export/publish check, or a quick play mode, could command a slow speed from rest with pushes disabled, so this shows up before a set ships.
- **Look at the forward-only share.** The base cfg has `rel_forward_envs=0.2` with forward-only commands clamped to `vx >= 0.3`, so a chunk of training never sees slow forward walking. I haven't verified this is the cause, though.
- **More episodes starting at rest.** Episodes that begin from a standstill with a small nonzero command would teach it to break into a walk at low speed.


Tested on `develop` @ `cb70b79`, `seed-v5`

record.author: notwitcheer
record.body:
Hi, thanks for microduck_rl. While training the rough velocity tasks (`Mjlab-Velocity-Rough-MicroDuck`, `Mjlab-VelStand-Rough-MicroDuck`) on an RTX 5090 I found two things in the terrain setup that change what the terrain curriculum does. Both are still present on `main` (cfe1c2a).

**1. `MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG` runs in random mode, so terrain levels are not a difficulty ladder**

`MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG` (`microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py`, line 127) does not set `curriculum`, and mjlab's `TerrainGeneratorCfg.curriculum` defaults to `False`. In random mode every patch samples a random sub-terrain and a random difficulty (`difficulty = self.np_rng.uniform(*self.cfg.difficulty_range)` in `mjlab/terrains/terrain_generator.py`), so rows are not ordered by difficulty. The `terrain_levels` curriculum then moves robots between rows of randomly rough patches, and `Curriculum/terrain_levels/mean` does not track terrain difficulty. mjlab's own rough velocity tasks turn curriculum mode on explicitly (`tasks/velocity/config/g1/env_cfgs.py` and `go1/env_cfgs.py`: `cfg.scene.terrain.terrain_generator.curriculum = True`).

**2. The play branch mutates the shared module-level config, which the training cfg also uses**

Each rough `make_*_env_cfg` assigns the module-level object directly (`cfg.scene.terrain.terrain_generator = MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG`), and its `if play:` branch then sets `curriculum = False`, `num_cols = 5`, `num_rows = 5` on that same object. Task registration builds the play cfgs too, so after `import mjlab_microduck.tasks` the training cfgs point at a 5 x 5 grid instead of the configured 10 x 20. Affected sites on `main`: `microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py` 753/772-774, `microduck_sitstand_env_cfg.py` 746-750, `microduck_standup_env_cfg.py` 842-846, `microduck_ground_pick_env_cfg.py` 608-612.

Repro (no GPU needed):

```python
import mjlab_microduck.tasks  # registers tasks, builds play cfgs
from mjlab_microduck.tasks import microduck_velstand_env_cfg as vs, microduck_velocity_env_cfg as vc

train = vs.make_microduck_velstand_env_cfg(rough=True).scene.terrain.terrain_generator
play = vs.make_microduck_velstand_env_cfg(play=True, rough=True).scene.terrain.terrain_generator
print(train.curriculum, train.num_rows, train.num_cols)  # False 5 5  (configured: rows 10, cols 20)
print(train is vc.MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG, train is play)  # True True
```

The dumped `params/env.yaml` of three of my rough training runs agrees: `curriculum: false`, `num_rows: 5`, `num_cols: 5`.

**Possible fix**

What I am testing locally on the velocity family: `deepcopy` the generator in each `make_*_env_cfg` (the module already imports `deepcopy`), and set `curriculum = True` for training while play keeps its 5 x 5 random grid on its own copy:

```python
cfg.scene.terrain.terrain_generator = deepcopy(MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG)
cfg.scene.terrain.terrain_generator.curriculum = not play
```

With that change, a 200-iteration run of `Mjlab-VelStand-Rough-MicroDuck` from the same checkpoint (4096 envs) dumps `curriculum: true`, `num_rows: 10`, and the terrain curriculum climbs: mean level 3.07 in the first 50 iterations to 4.43 in the last 50, with robots reaching row 9 after about 100 iterations. Without it, the same start stayed on a 5 x 5 grid with max level 4. (These runs use a tracking-based promote/demote rule in my fork rather than the stock distance rule, so the exact numbers will differ on `main`.)

I have not changed SitStand, StandUp or GroundPick rough locally, since restoring their 10 x 20 grid changes their training and I have not measured it. Happy to open a PR if that is useful.

record.author: mshooter
record.body:
The `<camera name="head_camera">` in `src/mjlab_microduck/robot/microduck/robot_allcollisions.xml`
(line 313 on develop at 08680d3, also in the other robot_*.xml variants) has `quat="0 0 -1 0"`. MuJoCo cameras
look along their own -Z, so at the reset pose it looks backwards into the head shell and renders a grey
image. Nothing in this repo renders from it, so training is unaffected; anyone rendering from the head
camera hits it.

Evidence:
- The runtime already knows the right frame: the `head_camera` site (line 312) composed with
  `SITE_TO_CV2` from microduck's `kinematics/src/head.rs` gives, in MuJoCo camera convention,
  look = -Z and up = +X in the head body frame. The `<camera>` element gives look = +Z, up = +Y..
- Setting the camera quat to `0.7071068 0 0 -0.7071068` matches that frame exactly; the rendered
  frame then shows the floor and horizon ahead.
- PRs #21 and #22 each overwrite `cam_quat` at load time to work around this (#22's README and
  `test_head_camera_optical_correction_...` describe it), and so does
  https://github.com/mshooter/microduck_academy (`smoke.py`, `CAMERA_QUAT_FORWARD`).

Two questions before a PR:
1. Is the file generated from a CAD export? If so the fix belongs in the export step.
2. The physical camera is mounted a quarter turn off and mediad leaves rotation to the consumer.
   Should the sim camera be upright (as above) or match the raw sensor?

Happy to send the one-line PR once you say which.

record.author: Rishitha2628
record.body:
Hi, thanks for open-sourcing microduck_rl, it's been great to learn from.

While training `Mjlab-BallKick-Flat-MicroDuck` on a laptop GPU I kept getting a PPO policy that kicks hard and then falls onto its back for the rest of the episode. Because it settles at roughly 40-57° of trunk tilt, the `fell_over` termination (`bad_orientation`, 70°) never fires, so the episode runs to time-out and the policy keeps most of the kick reward. Sharing in case it's useful; it may well be a known trade-off.

**Setup**
- repo at `cb70b79` (develop, 2026-09-14), no code changes (the run's saved git diff is empty)
- `uv run train Mjlab-BallKick-Flat-MicroDuck` with `--env.scene.num-envs 1024` (and one run at 2048), default agent config otherwise, right foot
- evaluation: exported ONNX, deterministic actions, 512 episodes, push curriculum held at stage 0; tilt measured the same way as `bad_orientation` (acos of projected gravity z)

**What I see**

| run | peak ball speed | trunk tilt at episode end | episodes ending upright (<30°) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PPO 1024 envs, seed 42, 1500 iters | 1.47 m/s | 57° | 0% |
| PPO 1024 envs, seeds 42/43/44, 300 iters | 1.47-1.60 m/s | 40-47° | 0% (3/3 seeds) |
| PPO 2048 envs, seed 42, 300 iters | 1.41 m/s | 36° | 0% |
| released `ball_kick_right.onnx` (microduck-policies) | 1.34 m/s | 1° | 100% |

In the 1500-iteration run the policy is already collapsing at iteration 100 and never recovers; the return keeps rising while the final lean gets worse. The training logs show it too: `Episode_Reward/upright` sits around 0.1 (weight 2.0) while `ball_forward_velocity` is ~11. It's also visible in `uv run play`.

**What I couldn't test:** the recommended 4096 envs (doesn't fit on my 6 GB GPU) or a run as long as the released policy's. So this may only show up at smaller batch sizes, which your released policy suggests.

**Possible fixes**, if it's worth closing:
- a lower `fell_over` limit for this task (something like 40-45°; the policies that stay up end at 1-3° of tilt, though I haven't measured the peak lean during the swing, so the right value needs checking), or
- a trunk-height termination (e.g. `root_height_below_minimum`), or
- gating/scaling the kick reward by uprightness after contact.

For comparison, an off-policy run (FastSAC, same env, 1024 envs) kicked at 1.40 m/s and stayed upright in 2 of 3 seeds, so the task is clearly learnable at this scale. Scripts, logs and videos are here if you want to reproduce: https://github.com/Rishitha2628/microduck-kick (see `docs/experiments.md`).

Happy to open a PR for whichever option you'd prefer.

**What I couldn't test:** the recommended 4096 envs (doesn't fit on my 6 GB GPU) or a run as long as the released policy's. So this may only show up at smaller batch sizes, which your released policy suggests.

**Possible fixes**, if it's worth closing:
- a lower `fell_over` limit for this task (something like 40-45°; the policies that stay up end at 1-3° of tilt, though I haven't measured the peak lean during the swing, so the right value needs checking), or
- a trunk-height termination (e.g. `root_height_below_minimum`), or
- gating/scaling the kick reward by uprightness after contact.

For comparison, an off-policy run (FastSAC, same env, 1024 envs) kicked at 1.40 m/s and stayed upright in 2 of 3 seeds, so the task is clearly learnable at this scale. Scripts, logs and videos are here if you want to reproduce: https://github.com/Rishitha2628/microduck-kick (see `docs/experiments.md`).

Happy to open a PR for whichever option you'd prefer.

record.author: nice-choi704
record.body:
Hi Pollen Robotics RL Team,

We are running controlled continued-training experiments on Microduck, including left-right symmetry ablations, on a local workstation. To compare against an exact official baseline rather than a different training lineage, we are looking for the original PyTorch checkpoint used to export the official walking policy.

## Target policy and documented provenance

Our archived official Hub file is:

- Repository: `pollen-robotics/microduck-policies`
- Revision: `1b56c396825c052a4e26e95cf2b8d8298af9e9b4`
- File: `alpha_walking.onnx`
- Size: 793,705 bytes
- SHA-256: `e36332d383997d51401897734cd3e79cf5038406feddb18b4d57ecfb141daa6c`

The same bytes were archived as `BEST_alpha_walking.onnx` from the official Microduck simulator. The repository documentation identifies this policy's source as W&B run `pollen-robotics/mjlab_microduck/441tzs6d`, checkpoint `model_3750.pt`.

## Why the ONNX export cannot provide an exact PPO resume

We reproduced the deterministic actor from the ONNX export, including its MLP weights and baked observation normalization, with zero output difference on 13,056 recorded observations.

However, the ONNX export does not preserve several checkpoint states needed to reproduce the original PPO state exactly:

- critic weights;
- Adam optimizer state;
- stochastic policy `distribution.std_param`;
- observation-normalizer sample `count`;
- training iteration and `common_step_counter`.

These values can be reinitialized or assumed, but they cannot be recovered exactly from the ONNX file. We therefore classify such a reconstruction as a new actor warm-start lineage, not a continuation of the official run.

As a local feasibility check, we trained only a fresh critic while keeping the reconstructed actor frozen. Our preregistered local validation gate remained unmet after 120 iterations (reported EV approximately 0.398 and NRMSE approximately 0.776, against thresholds of 0.80 and 0.45). We did not start PPO. These figures explain why we did not treat the reconstruction as an exact baseline resume; they are not intended as a general claim that actor warm-starting cannot work.

## Request

Our primary request is the exact checkpoint behind the archived walking policy:

- W&B run: `pollen-robotics/mjlab_microduck/441tzs6d`
- Checkpoint: `model_3750.pt`
- Supporting material, if available: checkpoint SHA-256, exact source commit, and saved environment and runner parameter files.

Separately, if current production checkpoints can be shared, we would also appreciate:

- W&B run: `pollen-robotics/mjlab_microduck/0045i2si`
- Checkpoint: `model_2749.pt`
- Documented source commit: `3750776`
- Saved environment and runner parameter files.

We understand that the v8 VelStand checkpoint belongs to a different task and training lineage and is not a substitute for `441tzs6d@3750` in an alpha-walking symmetry comparison.

A direct download, a Hugging Face artifact, or read-only W&B access sufficient to download the checkpoint would all work.

Thank you for open-sourcing the Microduck RL stack and for any guidance you can provide.

record.author: samoxis
record.body:
In `scene_apartment.xml` the stairwell (x ∈ [-0.40, 0.00], y ∈ [-1.40, -0.70]) has steps but no walls or bottom, and the floors around it are 1 cm slabs over empty space. A downward ToF beam that enters the hole at a shallow angle misses the steps, passes under the slab beyond, and hits nothing — so `sim/tof.py` reports status 255 ("nothing in range") where a real VL53L8CX would measure the stairwell's wall or bottom.

Repro, sensor at standing height over the north corridor, looking south:

```python
import numpy as np, mujoco
m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path("src/mjlab_microduck/robot/microduck/scene_apartment.xml")
d = mujoco.MjData(m); mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
g = np.zeros(1, dtype=np.int32)
for el in (8.4, 14.1, 19.7):                      # rows 5-7 of the 8x8 grid, head level
    e = np.radians(el); v = np.array([0, -np.cos(e), -np.sin(e)])
    print(el, mujoco.mj_ray(m, d, np.array([-0.2, -0.25, 0.246]), v, None, 1, -1, g))
# 8.4 -> 1.657 (floor beyond the hole)   14.1 -> -1.0   19.7 -> -1.0
```

Why it matters: a cliff guard developed in the simulator only ever sees the "nothing in range" signature of a drop; on the robot it would see a longer range instead. Both should be handled, but only one can be tested here.

A possible fix, five boxes lining the hole 0.6 m deep:

```xml
<geom name="well_bottom" type="box" size="0.20 0.35 0.005" pos="-0.20 -1.05 -0.605"/>
<geom name="well_n" type="box" size="0.20 0.005 0.30" pos="-0.20 -0.695 -0.30"/>
<geom name="well_s" type="box" size="0.20 0.005 0.30" pos="-0.20 -1.405 -0.30"/>
<geom name="well_w" type="box" size="0.005 0.35 0.30" pos="-0.405 -1.05 -0.30"/>
<geom name="well_e" type="box" size="0.005 0.35 0.30" pos="0.005 -1.05 -0.30"/>
```

With them the same beams read 1.186 m and 1.221 m (the south wall). Checked against `develop` @ 8d0db74 with MuJoCo directly; I haven't run the full training or the policies with the change.

Found while building a drop detector for an autonomy client: https://github.com/samoxis/microduck-brain (fixtures with these frames in `tests/fixtures/mujoco_drop.json`).

record.author: zfk0531
record.body:
你好！我在按你的飞特 HD-1910 版做复刻，目标是做一只能走路 + 有视觉/语音对话 + 接云端 LLM 的鸭子。
读了 microduck-replica 和 CAD 仓的文档，受益匪浅，有 4 个问题想请教（按我的下单优先级排序）。

## ① 打印材料与整机质量（最急，我要找打印服务下单）

你在 `imu-fix-1015` 里写「整鸭带电池 **806 g**，训练用 820 g，差 1.7%」。
我算了一下：官方 737.2 g + 15 只舵机各重 4.5 g ≈ 804.7 g，对得上。
我想让整机质量尽量贴近你那台，以便直接复用你的实机数据，所以想确认这个 806 g 的构成：

1. **是全 PLA，还是部分件用了铝合金增强？**
   CAD 仓 BOM 里「颈部 / 躯干底座 / 上腿加固板」标注了「可换铝合金增强」——
   你实际打的是塑料还是铝？
2. **填充率（infill）是多少？** 这在 Bambu Studio 的 3MF 里有预设，
   我要找打印服务商打（他们只收 STL，拿不到 3MF 参数），需要知道具体数值。
3. 层高 0.2 / 0.4 喷嘴 / PLA Basic 这几个参数，确认一下我没理解错。

另外：你的 3MF 是 09-15 版，v2.1 改了 TPU 合体轮胎。
**我们这种不做轮滑的版本，是不是直接按 09-15 那 52 个对象打就行？**

## ② 走路策略：重训还是调参

看到你 10-15 的记录里**收回了「舵机不行，要重训」**这个结论，
说「大家好多用他的跑通了」，元凶是 IMU 姿态模式（chip → gyro）。想确认现在的判断：

1. **现成 kissqy V167 策略 + 飞特舵机，是不是直接能走？** 还是要改动作缩放/滤波？
   （你的记录里用了「动作缩放 0.9、头滤波 0.5、腿滤波 0.7」）
2. **你 `software/training/` 里的 `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck-HD1910`，
   打算自己跑完整训练吗？** README 写「尚无本机实测通过的走路策略」
   「本次没有提交付费云端任务」。如果暂时不打算跑，我用 `--hf-jobs` 跑一版
   （官方说约 1–2 h / 十几元），训出来会发布回来给你。
3. 你提到「现有 Microduck 质量惯量仍是原版仿真值，后续需要按飞特实机数据校正」——
   **这个校正做了吗？** 还是仍用原版值？

## ③ HAT 板 / imu_to_dxl 板

看到 issue #25 有人问过套件，当时回答「舵机还没到」。现在应该到了，想再问一下：

1. **HAT 板 / imu_to_dxl 板有打样好的余量可转让吗？** 或者有没有拼单渠道？
   我们自己打样 4 层板 + SMT（113 个贴装位置、含 0603）起订量不划算。
2. 如果买不到，**嘉立创 PCBA 的 SMT 你走过吗？** 有没有踩过坑
   （哪些料要自己备、钢网要不要开）？

## ④ 舵机参数核对

你们和 LuwuDynamics 都用 `1910_m6.json`（`STS3215Actuator`）给 HD-1910 建模。想确认：

1. **HD-1910-C001 是否等同 HLS1910 / STS3215？** 飞特型号命名有点乱，
   XGO-Duck README 写 "HLS1910"，参数文件里写 `sts3215`。
   如果确认同族，我就直接沿用 `1910_m6.json`；否则要做系统辨识。
2. **规格书上的 10 kg·cm 是在几伏下测的？** `1910_m6.json` 里的 `kt` 隐含电压假设，
   我们总线是 6.6–8.2 V（满电 8.4 V），想核对匹配。
3. 减速比、编码器分辨率、回差这三项规格书上没有 —— **你们实测过吗？**

（注：你文档里说「参数不是本项目自行辨识的结果」，所以这条也许没人答得上来 ——
那我就直接沿用并做实机对照。）

---

另外提一下我的扩展方向，如果你也在做可以一起搞：
除了走路，我还要加**视觉 + 语音对话 + 云端 LLM**（大致是 Reachy Mini conversation app 那套）。
有两个硬件问题想请教：

1. **HAT 上麦克风和喇叭的间距，自播报时的回声（AEC）好消吗？**
   我想做声纹识别主人/家人，如果 AEC 做不好声纹就废了。
2. 摄像头装在头里，**你那边出图正常吗？** 官方代码 `--rotate` 默认 90，
   你记录里写「摄像头调整排线后在官方 B1 下出图」—— 是转 90 还是 180？

非常感谢！有问题我也会把结果反馈回来。

record.body:
### Description

Hi! I trained the Velocity and Roulade policies locally and ran into an issue when trying to visualize Roulade using the Viser browser viewer.

The native MuJoCo viewer works, but Viser crashes during initialization.

### Steps to reproduce

Run with a trained Roulade checkpoint:

```bash
uv run play Mjlab-Roulade-Flat-MicroDuck \
    --wandb-run-path ENTITY/PROJECT/RUN_ID \
    --viewer viser
```

### Error

```text
File "mjlab/tasks/velocity/mdp/velocity_command.py", line 166, in create_gui
    max_input = server.gui.add_slider(...)

File "viser/_gui_api.py", line 1900, in add_slider
    assert max >= value >= min

AssertionError
```

### Root cause

The Roulade environment uses very small velocity command ranges:

```python
command.ranges.lin_vel_x = (-0.01, 0.01)
command.ranges.lin_vel_y = (-0.01, 0.01)
command.ranges.ang_vel_z = (-0.05, 0.05)
```

However, `mjlab` creates joystick sliders with `min=0.1` and `initial_value=max_val`, which fails when `max_val < 0.1`.

### Suggested fix

Since Roulade doesn't need interactive velocity commands, one option is to skip joystick GUI creation for tasks with near-zero command ranges.

Alternatively, the slider initialization could be fixed upstream in `mjlab` to support smaller ranges.

I tested a workaround by overriding `VelocityCommandCommandOnly.create_gui()` to skip the joystick sliders when any upper bound is below `0.1`. **Viser now works correctly.**

```python
def create_gui(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
    """Skip joystick GUI for tasks with near-zero commands."""
    upper_bounds = (
        self.cfg.ranges.lin_vel_x[1],
        self.cfg.ranges.lin_vel_y[1],
        self.cfg.ranges.ang_vel_z[1],
    )

    if any(bound < 0.1 for bound in upper_bounds):
        return

    super().create_gui(*args, **kwargs)
```

### Environment

- Windows 10 + WSL2 (Ubuntu)
- Python 3.12
- NVIDIA RTX 5050 Laptop GPU
- `mjlab==1.3.0`
- `warp-lang==1.12.0`

Thanks for the great project!

# v8 velstand: inconsistent pure lateral starts and yaw drift in MuJoCo/Warp CPU

Hi, I am investigating inconsistent pure lateral motion with the released v8 `velstand.onnx` policy. This may be related to #59, although that report and its simulator results mainly concern v5.

I am reporting observations and asking for configuration guidance. I have not established a source-code defect or tested this on a physical robot.

## Environment

- Policy: `pollen-robotics/microduck-policies`, revision `v8`, `velstand.onnx`.
- Policy SHA256: `2fc7f8ee6acd7d0d3f66a99927b5d5a56589aeed02ec714de329b252d5ccf492`.
- Local base checkout: `b26950afb74432b53fe81c4d322988a3785ea0a6`, with local diagnostic changes.
- macOS / arm64; Warp CPU, no CUDA GPU.
- MuJoCo 3.10.0, mjlab 1.3.0, warp-lang 1.12.0, Torch 2.9.1, NumPy 2.4.1, ONNX Runtime 1.24.4.
- BAM pinned to `62bd8ce12154340be97e06f7f41a0ca8f116d967`.
- Physics 200 Hz; deterministic ONNX inference 50 Hz; 61 actor observations and 14 actions. The published policy weights were unchanged.

## Diagnostic setup and limitations

**This is a locally modified diagnostic configuration derived from VelStand, not an untouched upstream task.**

It uses flat terrain and the all-collisions/backlash robot with BAM. It starts upright at root z=0.125m / yaw=0, disables prone initialization and injected pushes, and fixes head/body commands to zero. Domain randomization, actor observation corruption and IMU mounting error are disabled; BAM voltage is 7.4V with drop gain 0.1. Physics uses 5ms implicitfast, 30 solver iterations and 50 line-search iterations. Physical command/sensor delays remain enabled.

The local wrapper also changes rewards, termination settings and critic observations; no training or critic inference was performed, and no falls or environment resets occurred during this probe.

The policy was evaluated directly in the mjlab/MuJoCo Warp environment, bypassing Studio, HTTP controls and robotd. No external heading controller or added yaw command was used. These results come from **three parallel environments with one seed (0)**, not three independent seeds.

## Command sequence

Command axes are `[vx, vy, vyaw]`; head/body commands remain zero:

1. Stand: `[0, 0, 0]` for 2s.
2. Left: `[0, +0.3, 0]` for 10s.
3. Stop for 3s.
4. Right: `[0, -0.3, 0]` for 10s.
5. Stop for 3s.
6. Left again: `[0, +0.3, 0]` for 10s.

## Observed results

Displacements and yaw excursions are measured relative to the trunk heading at the beginning of each segment. Maximum yaw is the largest absolute yaw departure during the entire 10s segment.

| Environment | Initial left displacement | Right displacement | Right maximum yaw excursion | Left after right displacement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | +0.0063m | -0.5302m | 13.40° | +0.4706m |
| 1 | +0.0062m | -0.5450m | 10.26° | +0.4435m |
| 2 | +0.4657m | -0.5375m | 16.54° | +0.0066m |

Three of the nine lateral segments barely moved; the other six did move. The main observations are inconsistent initiation and yaw drift under zero commanded yaw. I am not claiming that every segment is immobile or that a local acceptance threshold is an official requirement.

## Questions

1. Is reliable pure lateral motion from rest (`vx=0, vy=±0.3, vyaw=0`) expected with the released v8 VelStand policy?
2. Are there recommended scene, BAM, voltage, action-filtering or command settings for reproducing this checkpoint's lateral behavior?
3. Could the nominal evaluation changes or Warp CPU backend explain these observations? Is there a known-good upstream reproduction command/configuration to compare against?

I would like to verify configuration compatibility before attributing this to the policy or training recipe. The numerical report can be attached as `v8-lateral-observations.json`; its pass/fail fields use local diagnostic limits, not official criteria. The existing local probe depends on local configuration modules, so it is not yet a standalone upstream reproduction script.

[v8-lateral-observations.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33923720/v8-lateral-observations.json)
